cues.text: First, it finds the six risk classes. A risk class groups jobs by danger; riskier work pays more per hour.
Next, the hours worked, because the premium is charged per hour. One individual billed 504 more hours as a vendor.
Now it checks the official rules online, including each risk class. All twenty-four checks are confirmed, and five questions are left for a person.
Then it multiplies each class's hours by its rate: $111,469 in all. Employees pay a small share, but payroll took $504 too much.
Eight checks pass: every hour is accounted for.
Last, it writes the draft report and its workpapers.

All done. The draft shows $111,469 of premium for the quarter. Five items stay open: two questions about which risk class some staff belong in, $504 to refund to employees, a worker paid as a vendor, and the report itself, now past due. A person reviews, signs and files it; nothing is filed or paid yet.
